catalog_quote: There is little description of the metrical system by Peile or Valiquette but Kukatja broadly appears to follow many of the organisational principles described for many other Western Desert languages (see Wilmoth 2022: 87–89 for a recent summary): i) Primary stress falls on the first syllable of a prosodic word (directional prefixes and reduplicants constitute their own prosodic words) ii) A secondary stress will appear on the first syllable of disyllabic morphemes iii) Where it does not result in a stress clash based on (ii), a secondary stress will apply to alternating syllables after the primary stress iv) Final syllables are always unstressed ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is fixed on the first syllable of the prosodic word; the four directional prefixes (maa-, ngalya-, wati-, parra-) and reduplicants form their own prosodic words and carry their own primary stress. The marginal vowel-length contrast is confined to the primary-stressed (word-initial) syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the first syllable of each disyllabic (or longer) morpheme; otherwise on alternating syllables after the primary stress, avoiding clash; final syllables never stressed. Footnote 207 notes Tabain et al. 2014 found no phonetic correlates of secondary stress in Pitjantjatjara.
new_statements.exceptions: Directional prefixes and reduplicants are separate prosodic words with their own primary stress (A.1.1, A.4.2); a few reduplicated words have non-initial long vowels (e.g. kaarlkaarl-pungin). Author hedges that the metrical system is not yet studied in detail ('broadly appears to follow').
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the prosodic word (root plus suffixes; prefixes and reduplicants excluded as separate prosodic words); statement is impressionistic/descriptive, not instrumental. Describes 'older' Kukatja as spoken at Balgo (Wirrimanu), WA.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Kukatja as spoken at Balgo (Wirrimanu) and the Kutjungka region, WA = Glottolog kuka1246 / AIATSIS A68 / ISO kux, explicitly the 'older' variety. Not to be confused with Kukatja/Luritja C7 (NT, luri1234-type Western Desert variety) or Kokatha/Gugada C3 of South Australia (koka1244; Platt 1968/1972, which Glottolog mislists under kuka1246). PHOIBLE's 'Kukatja' inventory ER 2959 is actually drawn from Hansen & Hansen's Pintupi grammar (pint1250). Jones 2011 (also saved) describes neighbouring Wangkajunga (wang1288), not Kukatja.

sources.note: Appendix A.1.1 (p.415): primary stress on first syllable of the prosodic word (directional prefixes and reduplicants are their own prosodic words); secondary stress on first syllable of disyllabic morphemes, else alternating after primary; final syllables always unstressed. p.414: long vowels only in the primary-stressed (initial) syllable. A.4.2 pp.449-450: the four directional prefixes maa-, ngalya-, wati-, parra- each receive a primary stress. Notes Peile and Valiquette give little description of the metrical system.

Ennever 2024 points readers to this grammar for northern Western Desert.
